structured_output.summary: The wire chunk is correct, minimal and backed by executed evidence. profiles.rs repoints exactly the two CreateSecurityProfileRequest arguments (lines 91, 214) with frozen response roots and unchanged operation ids, proven byte-exactly. New wire tests cover create/update/list_for_token/list/get/paged list_all with defaults on and off, pre-auth rejection of 5 pointers x 3 invalid values (token.calls 0, wire.requests 0), raw-extension round-trips, typed-over-extension precedence and lossless null/unsupported responses; the 906-case pinned-Zod corpus agrees per root. All 107 recorded checks exit 0 on the reviewed source, including both compilers, the executed example, and the dependency audit ordered first. All four attempt-2 lows are genuinely fixed. Field semantics match the pinned upstream file exactly. Remaining issues are low: operation-matrix test bindings, one phase-27 regression-assertion gap, and PHASES.md detail.

findings.description: The ProfilesClient.create and ProfilesClient.update rows still bind only crates/scm-sdk/tests/management_contracts.rs::profile_methods_match_literal_routes_schemas_defaults_and_helpers (also contracts/native-operations.json:7691 and contracts/qualification.json:13942). Both rows carry the current profiles.rs digest 41d2aa05..., so a maintainer reading the operation matrix for the two methods whose request root actually changed is pointed only at the historical test, not at the four directional wire tests that qualify the change. The parity ledger's new wireTests list is the only binding.
findings.required_fix: Add the directional wire test references to the create/update rows in contracts/native-operation-mappings/management.json and regenerate contracts/native-operations.json and contracts/qualification.json.

findings.description: test_vendor_whitespace_is_excluded_from_all_new_hygiene_checks iterates range(21, 27), so phase 27's git diff --check commands are never asserted to carry :(exclude)contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0/* (appended at tools/check_phase.py:334-335). The receipt shows the exclusion present, but the named 'all new hygiene checks' invariant does not cover the active phase.
findings.required_fix: Extend the loop to include phase 27 and assert both the vendor and pinned-source exclusions for its git diff --check commands.

findings.description: PHASES.md states phase 26's acceptance requirements explicitly (lines 278-281) but gives phase 27 only one clause ('its model/wire qualification'). The phase-27-specific decisions - the red_team_management.py --check --current-source-compatibility mode, the required fresh current-source live receipt, and the deliberate deferral of clean extracted package consumers to phase 28 - exist only in docs/typescript-035-parity-plan.md and tools/check_phase.py comments.
findings.required_fix: Add a short phase-27 acceptance paragraph to docs/PHASES.md naming the current-source compatibility mode, the fresh read-only receipt requirement, and the package-consumer deferral.

evidence: crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/management/profiles.rs:91,214 are the only changed schema arguments ('typescript:0.35.0:CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema'); response roots at 76, 92, 107, 215, 231 and every .named() id are untouched. tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py:67-76 proves this byte-exactly against baseline 578f2e6 (before.count==2, after.count==2, after.replace(current,previous)==before, identical .named() lists).

Upstream parity verified directly against the pinned file: contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0/src/models/mgmt-security-profile.ts:239-246 (passthrough ContentTypeConfigurationSchema with the 4 optional protection keys), 262-269 (4 optional direction keys), 272-277 (ModelConfigurationSchema extends it plus 'enable-full-conversation-inspection': z.boolean().optional()), 288-289 ('content-type-mode': z.string().optional()), 334 and 368 (dlp_tenant_id: z.string().optional()). generated.rs:13372-13383 and 13493-13504 match these shapes, and docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:32-42 documents the non-enum mode exactly as upstream comments it.

limitations: Read-only review: I could not run git, cargo or the phase driver, so exit codes, test counts, source fingerprints and digest pins were read from docs/reviews/phase-27-chunk-wire-and-compatibility-attempt-03.checks.json and docs/checks/phase-27-rust-*-management.json rather than re-executed.
I recomputed no SHA-256, so parity-ledger sourceBindings, native-exports/qualification source digests and the live receipt hashes rest on the recorded passing owner checks that verify them.

I did not verify that the 107 recorded commands are literally equal to commands_for(27); review_phase.check_evidence:215 enforces that equality at record time and the receipt reports passed true with every exit_code 0.
Directional create/update were never exercised against a tenant; the current receipt verifies only OAuth token exchange and four 403 probes, as every document states.

Clean extracted package-consumer builds are deliberately excluded from commands_for(27) (tools/check_phase.py:319-323; management_consumers.py reports executionClaimed false). That evidence is phase 28 scope and I did not judge it.

I reviewed only the wire-and-compatibility chunk. Generated model and validation correctness was judged through the two compilers, selected generated declarations (generated.rs:13372-13604) and the independent oracle/fixture checks, not a full audit of the models-and-validation chunk.
I read neither .local/typescript nor any credential or tenant-registration material; contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0 as pinned was treated as the authoritative upstream input.

The new request roots reject null/wrong-type values the old passthrough accepted. The plan authorizes this and CHANGELOG.md:17-21 plus docs/STABILITY.md:36-48 disclose it in both directions, so I treated it as a recorded maintainer decision rather than a finding.
